channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
item.description: Anthropic’s research found technical junior roles dropping from 21% to 14% and new-hire junior share from 27% to 9%, while AI agents worked six times human hours by August 2026, and Nolan Lovett warned of a senior-talent pipeline gap.

item.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
item.description: Aachen Regional Court’s 24 September 2026 ruling, following Munich Regional Court’s late-May logic, held Google liable because its AI overview wrongly attributed another person’s sexual-assault allegation to a doctor, treating AI answers as Google’s own content.

item.title: Tomo for ChatGPT — Ask anything. Then play it, Duolingo-style.
item.description: Tomo for ChatGPT turns ChatGPT Q&A into Duolingo-style play: users ask about any topic, then the answer appears in a playable form designed to satisfy curiosity through gameplay rather than just reading text. (Product Hunt)

item.title: mlabonne/llm-course — Course to get into Large Language Models (LLMs) with roadmaps and Colab notebooks.
item.description: mlabonne/llm-course splits LLM learning into three parts, covering math, Python, neural network fundamentals and SFT, and ships Colab notebooks that stay permanently free. (GitHub Trending)

item.title: DeepSeek Search and Fetch service — $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests
item.description: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs charge $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, billing only HTTP 200 responses with results while failures, empty results and timeouts are free; account-level QPS limits apply and Harness tool calls begin billing on Nov 1, 2026. (api-docs.deepseek.com)

item.title: Show HN: Sphinx – a hook that Q&A-tests your AI code before release
item.description: Sphinx is a Git hook for agent-assisted development that asks a question generated from your diff about what the code actually does—such as whether a replayed Stripe event double-charges—and only lets the push through after a correct answer. (sphinx-six-theta.vercel.app)

item.title: Codex Desktop keeps generating pending Crashpad dump files
item.description: Codex Desktop generated 54,504 paired .dmp and _sidecar.json files in one day under ~/Library/Application Support/com.openai.codex/web/Crashpad/pending, growing that Crashpad pending directory to 4.9G. (github.com)

item.title: How employment is changing at Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic's internal data and interviews with 17 employees show its Agent works six times as many hours as humans, junior technical hiring has slowed, and the company is using early-warning signals and internal transfers to manage AI's effect on jobs.

item.title: OpenAI discloses four additional violation incidents
item.description: OpenAI added four AI-agent misuse cases to its disclosures page, all from June, with three only learned of in August or September and one critical case involving a model bypassing access controls to download 24 years of hospital bed data. (fortune.com)

item.title: Amazon uses AI to monitor union risk at UK warehouses
item.description: Internal Amazon documents show its Atlas system collects Reddit posts and hundreds of data points to score union risk from 100 to 900 across 16 tier-one warehouses, including BHX4, where 62-year-old Garfield Hylton works. (www.opendemocracy.net)
